_README: Goldened two-layer shim gap inventory. See test/shim-surface.test.cjs for what
this is and why it is a reviewed MAP rather than a must-be-empty gate.
Regenerate with UPDATE_GOLDEN=1, and add a note below for anything new.
Measured against the EXTRACTED cli.cjs (~21MB), never the 255MB Bun binary.

_notes.crypto.X509Certificate: LEFT layer2_node_apis_missing 2026-11-23: libexec/node-shim/internal/x509.cjs implements the constructor (PEM then DER, OpenSSL error codes), raw, serialNumber, fingerprint256, validFrom/validTo(+Date), ca, toString and toJSON, held to host node by test/node-shim-x509.test.cjs over every node root. Every other member exists and THROWS by name (subject, issuer, subjectAltName, publicKey, checkIssued, verify, ...). Why it mattered: 2.1.330's CA-trust builder does `new X509Certificate(pem).raw` per bundled root and logged `CA certs: A bundled root does not parse: TypeError: not a function` 16x per session; its two other read sites (validTo + checkIssued, subject) sit inside try/catch, so a wall there degrades as the absent class did.
_notes.layer1_bun_props_missing_deferred: NEW drift (2026-09-02), seen for the first time only once this suite could stage a real provider — see BACKLOG.md's 'Bun.zstdDecompress / Bun.zstdDecompressSync are new golden-map drift, unreviewed'. Upstream's own embedded-text-asset reader (43 OTHER modules reference the chunk that defines it), so this is NOT a narrow one-off like Bun.ant or zlib.createZstdDecompress above, and per that entry it MUST NOT be added to the main golden list or stubbed without the same reachability work those got first. Listed HERE, separately, so `layer1_bun_props_missing` keeps asserting on any OTHER new drift while these two specific, already-triaged entries do not block the suite. Move to the main list (with a note) once reviewed, or implement a real stub and remove.
_notes.intl: NOT a node builtin — libexec/node-shim/modules/intl.cjs backs the Intl GLOBAL, not a require()able module, so neither side can enumerate it by name. Allowed, not a gap.
_notes.Bun.SQL: FIXED (no longer a layer1 gap, kept as history). Was an ACTIVE DIVERGENCE: upstream guards it with `if (typeof Bun > "u") throw Error("claude gateway requires the native binary")`, TRUE under real node ("undefined" > "u") but FALSE under quaude because bun-shim defines a Bun global at all — so the guard was defeated and `new Bun.SQL(...)` produced a bare `Bun.SQL is not a constructor` instead. bun-shim.cjs now gives Bun.SQL a throwing constructor that hands back upstream's own message verbatim. Reachability: confirmed NOT on the -p/interactive routes — Bun.SQL is used only inside the `claude gateway --config <path>` subcommand (a separate commander-registered enterprise auth/telemetry server), the sole call site in the bundle. See test/bun-shim-sql-guard.test.cjs.
_notes.Bun.WebView: BENIGN, and a good example of the shape we want: guarded by `"WebView" in Bun`, correctly false under the shim, so the branch is skipped and the function returns false. Feature detection that works. UNMEASURABLE, not merely unreached: CLODE_SHIM_PROBE (libexec/node-shim/internal/probe.cjs) wraps only node:* builtins loaded through loader.cjs's loadBuiltin() (its sole installProbe call site is loader.cjs:231) — libexec/bun-shim.cjs (the Bun.* global / bun: modules) has no probe instrumentation at all. This layer1 gap can never be armed by any corpus under the current probe design, so the BENIGN verdict above rests on code audit alone, not on measured reachability. See test/shim-surface/reachability.json's `probe_scope_limitation` and `unmeasurable` fields.
_notes.Bun.Image: REVIEWED 2026-09-26, at the pin bump to 2.1.283 (0 references in the 2.1.251 darwin-arm64 carve; in 2.1.283, 3 on the darwin-arm64 carve and 1 on the linux and win32 carves). Two, darwin only, are the clipboard entry points (`Bun.Image.hasClipboardImage()` / `Bun.Image.fromClipboard()`), each inside try/catch with a false/null fallback: no image paste, the honest answer here. The third, on every carve, is NEW and NOT guarded at its site: the image-processor factory (`jee()`) now hands back `(e)=>new Bun.Image(...)`, where 2.1.251 (`yz()`) loaded a native processor, then sharp, neither of which ever loaded under quaude. Its six call sites, read 2026-09-26 on the darwin-arm64 carve (minified names from it): the image-resize function (`AAe`) and one other (`L`) catch the throw and fall back (the original bytes when the header dimensions and the base64 size fit the API limits, else a user-facing "Unable to resize image" error); the clipboard read converts a BMP inside its own try/catch; three (`qPr`, the pasted-file BMP conversion `kio`, and `cu` in another module) are not guarded at their own sites, and whether their callers catch is NOT verified. So under quaude image processing is unavailable, as it was on 2.1.251 (not re-verified site by site): a standing divergence from native, which resizes and converts. Implementing it means an image codec in the engine; filed in BACKLOG.md, not attempted here.
_notes.Bun.FetchSession: BENIGN, reviewed 2026-09-26: new in 2.1.283 (0 references in the 2.1.278 binary). One read, feature-detected, in the mTLS module (`let e=typeof Bun>"u"?void 0:Bun.FetchSession;if(!e)return;`), and its one caller falls back to the plain fetch path when that returns nothing. Absent == a host without it. Also accepted by name in libexec/inspect-claude-bundle.cjs ACCEPTED_UNRECOGNIZED_BUN; do not stub it (a stub flips the detection).
_notes.bun:jsc: BENIGN. One site: `try { let {heapStats} = await import("bun:jsc") ... } catch {}` for heap diagnostics. The rejection is caught, so a missing module degrades to no heap stats, matching any non-Bun host. UNMEASURABLE, not merely unreached: same probe-scope limitation as Bun.WebView above — libexec/bun-shim.cjs is not instrumented by CLODE_SHIM_PROBE, so this layer1 gap can never be armed by any corpus regardless of whether the bundle reaches it. See test/shim-surface/reachability.json's `probe_scope_limitation` and `unmeasurable` fields.
_notes.bun:sqlite: DRIFT, not a gap: bun-shim declares an interceptor for it in PROVIDES but bundle 2.1.218 never imports it. Harmless dead weight; listed so the declaration's drift stays visible instead of silently accumulating.

DECLARED WALLS — the same ones test/node-shim-wall-tripwires.test.cjs alarms on, rediscovered here independently without being told they exist. That rediscovery is the main evidence this map works. They throw branded node-shim errors rather than failing silently. MEASURED (phase 2 Task 4, reachability.json dated 2026-08-04 against bundle 2.1.218): unarmed across all three corpora that ran (apicheck, agentic, interactive) — see reachability.json's `unarmed` list. This is corpus coverage, not a clean negative: per reachability.json's `corpus_blind_spots`, agentic runs against a MOCKED Anthropic server so it structurally cannot exercise real TLS/HTTP client paths; apicheck's credentialed branch hung (RECIPE.md G6, see the crypto.* note below) before reaching whatever lies past it; interactive captures only a 10s no-keystroke initial paint (no typed turn, no tool use).
_notes.crypto.*: The largest cluster (X509Certificate, createPrivateKey/PublicKey, createSign/createVerify, sign, pbkdf2/pbkdf2Sync, KeyObject). MEASURED (phase 2 Task 4, reachability.json dated 2026-08-04 against bundle 2.1.218): unarmed across every corpus that ran (apicheck, agentic, interactive) — see reachability.json's `unarmed` list and `unarmed_meaning`. NAMED BLIND SPOT, not evidence of unreachability: the ONLY corpus that even attempts the credentialed branch — apicheck's -p items, seeded that run with a COPY of a real ~/.claude/.credentials.json, deleted immediately after — HUNG on the quaude side before completing a turn (naude: exit 0 both items; quaude: apicheck's own 60s timeout fired, status:143). This reproduces RECIPE.md G6 (previously believed darwin-ppc/Darwin-8-specific) on darwin-arm64 — see reachability.json's `apicheck` corpus entry (`note`, `perItem`). The crypto.* cluster is exactly where credentialed token-refresh / enterprise-auth (mTLS, Vertex/Bedrock) handling would live, so "unarmed" here means "we could not get far enough down the credentialed path to find out", NOT "the path does not use them". RECIPE.md G4 already flags that auth path as unverified. Phase-3's recommended next step (reachability.json's `phase3_recommendation`) is an isolated HOME seeded with a syntactically-valid FIXTURE credentials file — unrelated to any real account — to take the credentialed branch deliberately and safely, without hanging and without borrowing a real token.
_notes.fs.fchmodSync / fs.fstat / fs.ReadStream: FIXED (no longer layer2 gaps, kept as history). Were fd-flavored variants of things the shim DOES provide by path (chmodSync, statSync, createReadStream) — same class as the FileHandle.chmod gap that broke Edit, which is precisely why this map exists. fchmodSync now tracks fd->path at fs.openSync/close and chmods that path (no fd-based fchmod primitive in the sync-fs patch, same strategy FileHandle.chmod already used); fstat routes through the existing fstatSync via cbWrap; ReadStream is now a real class fs.createReadStream() constructs, not a lookalike. See test/node-shim-fs-fd-variants.test.cjs.
_notes.fs.watch: test/fidelity/RECIPE.md row C7 remains UNVERIFIED — nothing in this file or in reachability.json answers it; do not read the absence of an `fs.watch` entry anywhere in this measurement as a clean result. fs.watch is not a golden gap at all: it is a PRESENT property on the shim's fs, a never-firing stub (`fsMod.watch` in libexec/node-shim/modules/fs.cjs), verified `'watch' in fs === true` and `typeof fs.watch === 'function'`. CLODE_SHIM_PROBE fires ONLY on ABSENT properties (`!(prop in target)`, libexec/node-shim/internal/probe.cjs lines 39 and 45) — so an access to a PRESENT-but-stubbed API like this one structurally cannot arm the probe in either direction, and grepping reachability.json for "fs.watch" always comes back empty, proving nothing about reachability. This probe is structurally blind to PRESENT-BUT-STUBBED APIs generally, not just this one. Answering C7 needs a different instrument: a logging wrapper on the EXISTING stub recording whether any of its four known bundle call sites (jobStateNameSync, useBgSessionPr, an unref'd private-field watcher, vendored chokidar) ever arms a listener on the -p / interactive routes.
_notes.child_process.fork / ChildProcess: fork() has no meaning under tjs (no node child bootstrap). If a reachable path ever forks, that is a design question, not a missing function. Per reachability.json's `corpus_blind_spots`, agentic's four scripted flows (Bash, Edit, Workflow, subagent, MCP-ws) do not exercise child_process.fork by construction — a coverage gap in the corpus, not a confirmed absence in the bundle. Not probed on the credentialed apicheck path either (hung at G6, see crypto.* note above).

_notes.http.request / https.request: REMOVED from layer2 on 2026-08-22 because they are now IMPLEMENTED (libexec/node-shim/modules/http.cjs, client section; characterized in test/node-shim-http-client.test.cjs). Kept as history because WHY matters: this map listed them as gaps, and the companion wall-tripwire declared them latent, but neither could say whether upstream REACHED them. Measurement (instrumented shim + blobulated quaude + driven flows) said: not on the default Anthropic backend (axios picks its XHR adapter under tjs, because txiki defines a global XMLHttpRequest), but YES on Bedrock — 10 http.request calls at the EC2 instance metadata service from the AWS SDK credential chain, and an https.request at bedrock.<region>.amazonaws.com from @smithy/node-http-handler. That is the shape of evidence this map is meant to prompt, and it is why the entry is gone rather than annotated.
_notes.net.createServer / net.connect: STILL A GAP (net.createServer present since 2026-11-18 only as a stub that throws, naming the gap), and the reason npm `ws` cannot connect under quaude: ws's initAsClient unconditionally passes `createConnection` to http.request, so it never uses the shim client's own socket. The shim client refuses that option by name (ERR_SHIM_HTTP_UNSUPPORTED_OPTION) rather than ignoring it. Closing this means a real net.Socket, which is a bigger job than the HTTP client was.
_notes.SCANNER REBUILD 2026-08-29: The layer-2 list moved because the SCANNER was repaired, not because upstream suddenly reached for new APIs. From 2.1.243 upstream ships a code-split ESM graph and emits ZERO require() for builtins (measured: 0 aliases for fs, os, path, crypto, net, http, child_process, stream, util, tty, v8 - every module but worker_threads), so layer2Gaps `continue`d past every module and reported NO GAPS AT ALL. The 16 entries below were stale 2.1.218 measurements that survived only because the golden test asserts layer 1 first and died on Bun.ant before reaching layer 2. The companion canary ("the scanner still finds the known fs.watch call sites") went red and stayed red for weeks as a tolerated baseline; it was right, and it was the only thing standing between this map and silent uselessness. Repaired in three steps, all in shim-surface/bundle-refs.cjs: read graph.json sources (real strings) instead of the escape-laden graph runner; learn ESM's three binding shapes (import*as X / import X / import{prop as x}); and resolve bindings MODULE-SCOPED, because minified names are one character and a bundle-wide lookup made every `n.abort()` evidence for `process.abort` (10 such phantoms, now gone).
_notes.util.getSystemErrorName: FIXED 2026-08-29 (no longer a layer2 gap, kept as history). Two of the eight NEWLY VISIBLE entries above were triaged the day the repaired scanner surfaced them; this is the one that got implemented. Upstream's single import site is the dirSync anchor module (`import{getSystemErrorName as vn,promisify as gt}from"util"`), whose only call reads darwin's __error() through bun:ffi and renders `code: vn(-b)` when an *at() syscall fails. MEASURED reachability, correcting the triage that sent this task out: that call site is behind the bun:ffi WALL, not on the credentials-store path — libexec/bun-shim.cjs's `bun:ffi` provides a dlopen() that throws, upstream catches it inside Bn() and sets the anchor to null ("dirSync anchor: bun:ffi unavailable"), so vn is never called today. Implemented anyway, and the Bun.ant reasoning is exactly why the two decisions differ: nothing FEATURE-DETECTS getSystemErrorName, so providing it advertises no capability we cannot honor, and the alternative was the interop facade's lazy thrower firing at the precise moment an errno was being named. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE, because the obvious one is wrong: node answers from LIBUV's error map, not from os.constants.errno, and on darwin/arm64 the two disagree on 18 of 79 names (EWOULDBLOCK must answer "EAGAIN"; EOPNOTSUPP/ECHILD/EDEADLK/... must answer "Unknown system error -N"). The shim asks the engine's own libuv via `new tjs.Error(n).code` (= uv_err_name), so no table is transcribed. Differential-locked against host node by test/node-shim-system-error-name.test.cjs.
_notes.zlib.createZstdDecompress: INTENTIONAL GAP, decided 2026-08-29, same shape as Bun.ant above and pinned by test/zlib-zstd-stream-gap.test.cjs. Upstream's single import site is the NATIVE release downloader (`import{createZstdDecompress as rt}from"zlib"` beside `var xe="https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases"`): it streams `${base}/${version}/${platform}/${file}.zst` through `pipeline(res.data, hashTap, rt(), sizeTap, fileStream)`. NOT the sync zstd clode already provides — that one is a HOST TOOL (libexec/host-provision.cjs + bun-graph.cjs shell out to zstd/unzstd/zstdcat at CARVE time, so a target never needs zstd to read upstream's embedded text assets). This is a streaming node:zlib Transform, and tjs has no native zlib at all (see libexec/node-shim/modules/zlib.cjs). MUST NOT BE STUBBED: upstream would then pipeline through a Transform that emits nothing or throws mid-download, turning "no zstd" into a corrupt or hung install; and unlike the sync path there is nothing to shell out to inside a pipeline. UNREACHABLE, for two INDEPENDENT reasons, both of which the pin asserts: (1) the downloader is only entered from the native updater / `claude update` install dispatch, and clode neutralizes all three updater widgets plus the manual dispatch; (2) upstream's installation type can only resolve to "native" inside `if(Al())`, and `Al()` is `typeof Bun<"u"&&Bun.isStandaloneExecutable===!0` — bun-shim reports that false, so QZ() returns "unknown" and the native widget is never mounted. If either wall falls, the gap becomes a live download failure and the decision must be re-taken.
_notes.zlib.createBrotliDecompress: INTENTIONAL GAP, decided 2026-11-22 (the NetBSD/arm64 /login failure). Its one reader is the bundle's axios: `Hr=typeof Le.createBrotliDecompress==="function"` decides whether the request offers br, and the response decoder uses it when the server answers br. The engine has no brotli decoder; while the shim exposed this as a present-but-throwing function, axios offered br, Cloudflare answered the OAuth token exchange in br, the decoder threw, and sign-in said "Couldn't get an answer from the sign-in service". ABSENT, axios offers gzip/deflate, which node-shim's zlib now decodes for real (libexec/node-shim/modules/zlib.cjs, over the engine's inflate). Pinned by test/zlib-axios-oracle.test.cjs ("zlib offers brotli only if it can decode it"). Implement a real decoder, then remove this entry.
_notes.NEWLY VISIBLE 2026-08-29 (os.devNull, fs: NOT new upstream behaviour and NOT yet reviewed - these are what the repaired scanner can see that the broken one could not. Each is a SINGLE import site (counts: os.devNull 2, the rest 1 apiece; fs.writev is one bare read), which is why the old require()-only scan missed them even before 2.1.243 went ESM. The 72 raw `fork(` substrings in the bundle are other objects' methods. Kept as history because the entry was true against 2.1.218.
_notes.Bun.ant: NO LONGER A LAYER-1 GAP as of 2026-09-24, because the property now EXISTS: upstream 2.1.278 added Bun.ant.CellSegmenter, the TUI's screen model, which it constructs unconditionally, so bun-shim provides Bun.ant with EXACTLY that one member (pinned by test/bun-shim-ant-gap.test.cjs; contract in test/bun-shim-cell-segmenter.test.cjs). Everything below still holds for the OTHER members, which stay absent. ORIGINAL NOTE: INTENTIONAL DIVERGENCE, decided 2026-08-29 with the reasoning in libexec/bun-shim.cjs (beside spawnSync) and pinned by test/bun-shim-ant-gap.test.cjs. NEW in 2.1.243: Anthropic's own private Bun namespace, four syscall-backed methods — getPeerUid(fd)/getPeerPid(fd) (SO_PEERCRED / LOCAL_PEERCRED on a unix socket), setDumpable(bool) (Linux prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE,0)), memoryPressureLevel() (macOS). MUST STAY ABSENT, not stubbed: upstream gates a capability on `typeof Bun.ant?.getPeerPid === "function"`, so any stub — throwing or not — flips that probe true and advertises a peer-credential capability the shim cannot honor. That is the Bun.SQL trap in reverse. Absent is the faithful answer and the probe currently gets the RIGHT one. NOT IMPLEMENTED, checked rather than assumed: peer credentials are technically in reach (vendored txiki.js exposes socket_from_fd(fd) and sock.getopt() in mod_posix-socket.c), but BOTH call sites sit behind declared node-shim walls that throw first — net.connect for the UDS client, the missing net.Server for the daemon — so implementing them means implementing behind a closed door. setDumpable and memoryPressureLevel have no txiki primitive at all (prctl: zero hits in the source). OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOUR, and it is NOT uniformly graceful, which is why the walls are load-bearing rather than incidental: the capability probe degrades cleanly (upstream drops the capability); the macOS background low-memory probe degrades cleanly (lowMem reads false, so background sessions never retire early for memory pressure; non-macOS uses os.freemem() and is unaffected); Linux setDumpable reports "prctl unavailable" and the process stays dumpable, one hardening step short of upstream; but the daemon peer-uid check FAILS OPEN (catch -> null -> upstream reads "no objection"), and the UDS client peer-pid check REFUSES TO SEND outright ("endpoint-unverifiable"). Both of those are unreachable only because net.connect and net.Server throw first. test/bun-shim-ant-gap.test.cjs asserts both walls and goes RED the day either comes down, which is when this decision must be re-taken.
_notes.crypto.createCipheriv / crypto.createDec: BENIGN (a cache that stays empty), reviewed 2026-09-26: new in 2.1.283, one module (the MCP discovery cache, merged into __clode-scc-1.js on the darwin-arm64 carve) that seals each cached entry with AES-256-GCM and opens it again. The cache is OFF unless the MCP_DISCOVERY_CACHE env flag or its remote kill-switch gate turns it on. Every write runs inside the cache's serialized-write wrapper, whose `.catch` logs "discovery-cache: write op failed" (all three write sites, read from the carve), and the open is inside its own try/catch, so under quaude, where both are absent, a write throws and is logged, nothing is ever cached, and every MCP server's tools are discovered live: the path with the cache off. Not driven.

_notes.fs.exists: A SCANNER FALSE POSITIVE, read 2026-11-21: the three reads are `s.exists=...` on a TypeScript project-service object in the vendored TypeScript language service (chunk-mk44m07h.js), where a binding of fs shares the minified name. Nothing calls fs.exists.
_notes.GLOBAL process NOW SCANNED (2026-11-22): shim-surface/bundle-refs.cjs's scan never saw a GLOBAL builtin: `process` is never imported, so no process.* member was ever on this map. 2.1.330 relaunches itself through process.execve (`/tui classic`), node-shim had none, and the spawnSync fallback left the terminal dead (P0, NetBSD/arm64, 2026-11-22) while this map stayed silent. Every module now binds the global `process`. process.execve is implemented (node-shim process.cjs, engine __tjs_execve) and, proven by hand, this gate names it as a NEW gap when the shim drops it. Of the nine other members the scan newly saw, process.title is now implemented (the executable path, as native answers); the remaining eight are listed in the entries below, each read on the 2.1.330 carve.
_notes.process.getgid / geteuid / getegid / get: FEATURE-DETECTED at every 2.1.330 site read 2026-11-22 (`process.getgid?.()`, `typeof process.geteuid==="function"?process.geteuid():process.getuid?.()`, `process.getgroups?.()??[]`, `process.getegid?[process.getegid()]:[]`): the permission/ownership checks (sockets dir, consent-store canonicalization, managed-settings and setgid-folder tests) fall back to getuid or to no group, as on a platform without them. Not a silent wrong answer, but a narrower one than node's (no gid/egid/groups): implementing them wants the engine's uv_os_get_passwd/getgid, BACKLOG candidate.
_notes.process._getActiveHandles / _getActiveRe: The heap-dump diagnostics (chunk-g0392cxd.js, beside v8.getHeapStatistics above): called UNGUARDED, so that diagnostic throws here, the same path v8.getHeapStatistics already marks as unsupported. Not on the -p or interactive turn routes.
_notes.process.dlopen: A native-addon loader via /proc/self/fd (chunk-vw137skj.js), inside try/catch: a node addon cannot load into quaude at all, so its throw is the honest answer and is caught.
_notes.process.title: IMPLEMENTED 2026-11-22 (kept as history): newly seen by the global-process scan; node-shim now answers the executable's path, as Bun 1.4.4 does under 2.1.330, and stores assignments (no OS process rename).
_notes.process.threadCpuUsage: FEATURE-DETECTED (`process.threadCpuUsage?.()??process.cpuUsage()`): falls back to cpuUsage, which node-shim answers from the engine's rusage.
_notes.fs/promises.glob: NEW 2026-11-25 (2.1.332; first measurable once subpath modules were enumerated): the SDK agent toolset's glob tool binds `Kt=w.glob` (import*as w from "fs/promises") and iterates Kt(pattern,{cwd,withFileTypes:true,exclude}). Absent in the shim, so that tool fails "not a function" under quaude; the CLI's own Glob tool does not use it. A real gap, not tolerated as harmless: BACKLOG.md, '2.1.332 reaches for two node APIs the shim lacks'.
_notes.dns/promises.Resolver: NEW 2026-11-25 (2.1.332): the Datadog sender's offline check, `new Resolver({timeout:1000,tries:1}).resolve4(host)` in try/catch, offline only on code ENOTFOUND. Absent, the constructor throws and the check reads ONLINE, so telemetry is attempted as on a connected box. Harmless until offline: BACKLOG.md, '2.1.332 reaches for two node APIs the shim lacks'.
